1: The book's purpose: to give wisdom and discipline. "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge." A father warns his son against joining a gang, and Wisdom calls out in the streets.
Wisdom starts with reverence for God, and with choosing your friends.
2: If you seek wisdom as you would silver, you will find the knowledge of God. It will protect you from evil men and from adultery.
Wisdom is a gift that has to be sought.
3: "Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding." Honour God with your wealth. The Lord corrects those he loves.
God's direction is better than our own cleverness.
4: A father passes on what his father taught him. "Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life."
What we let into our heart shapes our whole life.
5: The seductress's lips drip honey, but the end is bitter. "Rejoice in the wife of your youth."
Faithfulness in marriage is the wise path and the happy one.
6: Do not guarantee another's debt. "Go to the ant, you sluggard." Seven things the Lord hates. Adultery is fire carried in the lap.
Practical wisdom about money, work and purity.
7: A scene: at dusk a married woman lures a foolish young man, who follows "like an ox to the slaughter".
Temptation is described so that it can be recognised and avoided.
8: Wisdom calls at the city gates. She was with God before the world began, his delight day by day.
The Church reads this of Christ, the Wisdom of God, and applies it to Our Lady in the liturgy.
9: Lady Wisdom has built her house and set her table: "Come, eat of my bread." Lady Folly calls too: "Stolen water is sweet."
Everyone accepts one invitation or the other.
10: Short two-line proverbs contrasting the wise and the foolish, the diligent and the lazy, careful and careless speech.
11: A false balance is an abomination to the Lord. The generous person prospers; pride comes before disgrace.
Honesty and generosity pay; hoarding does not.
12: Whoever loves discipline loves knowledge. A good wife is her husband's crown. Truthful lips endure.
13: "Whoever walks with the wise becomes wise." Hope deferred makes the heart sick. A father who loves his child disciplines him.
We become like the company we keep.
14: "There is a way that seems right to a man, but its end is the way of death." Whoever oppresses the poor insults his Maker.
Feeling right is not the same as being right.
15: "A soft answer turns away wrath." Better a dinner of herbs where love is than a fattened ox with hatred.
How we speak decides whether conflict grows or dies.
16: "The heart of man plans his way, but the Lord establishes his steps." Pride goes before destruction.
Make plans, and hold them humbly.
17: "A friend loves at all times." Even a fool who keeps silent is thought wise. A cheerful heart is good medicine.
18: "Death and life are in the power of the tongue." To answer before listening is folly. The name of the Lord is a strong tower.
19: "Whoever is generous to the poor lends to the Lord." Many are the plans in a man's mind, but the Lord's purpose stands.
God counts kindness to the poor as a loan to himself.
20: "Wine is a mocker." Diverse weights are an abomination. Even a child is known by his actions.
21: The king's heart is in the Lord's hand. Doing justice is more acceptable than sacrifice.
22: "A good name is to be chosen rather than great riches." Train up a child in the way he should go. Thirty sayings of the wise begin.
23: Do not crave a ruler's delicacies or wear yourself out to get rich. A vivid picture of the drunkard. "Buy truth, and do not sell it."
Moderation at table and with money.
24: A just man falls seven times and rises again. The field of the sluggard is overgrown with thorns.
Falling is not final; staying down is.
25: "A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold." If your enemy is hungry, give him bread.
Paul quotes the saying about feeding your enemy.
26: Portraits of the fool, the lazy man who says "There is a lion in the street", and the gossip. Without wood a fire goes out.
27: "Let another praise you, and not your own mouth." Faithful are the wounds of a friend. Iron sharpens iron.
Real friends tell us the truth.
28: "The wicked flee when no one pursues." Whoever conceals his sins will not prosper; whoever confesses and forsakes them obtains mercy.
A plain statement of why confession matters.
29: One who is often reproved and stiffens his neck will be broken. Where there is no prophetic vision the people cast off restraint.
A society needs God's word to hold together.
30: "Give me neither poverty nor riches." Lists of four: things never satisfied, things too wonderful, small creatures that are wise.
A prayer for enough, and wonder at creation.
31: A queen mother's advice to her son, then a poem in praise of a capable wife: hard-working, generous to the poor, wise in speech.
"Charm is deceitful and beauty is vain, but a woman who fears the Lord is to be praised."
